title: Accenture Technology Vision 2024: Human by design: How AI unleashes the next level of human potential
notes: Four trends ('Make It Human—the 2024 Trends'). Web page dated January 9, 2024. Labels and descriptions from the web page; the full PDF (also live) says 'For more than 20 years, Accenture has developed the Technology Vision report'. No edition-level horizon. Edition-level survey: 95% of executives agree that making technology more human will massively expand the opportunities of every industry.

entries.label: A match made in AI
entries.quote: People are asking generative AI chatbots for information – transforming the business of search today, and the futures of software and data-driven enterprises tomorrow.
entries.subject: Generative AI chatbots and enterprise knowledge (LLM advisors)
entries.note: Printed subtitle: 'Reshaping our relationship with knowledge'. Survey: 95% of executives believe generative AI will compel their organization to modernize its technology architecture (no horizon).

entries.label: Meet my agent
entries.quote: AI is taking action, and soon whole ecosystems of AI agents could command major aspects of business.
entries.subject: AI agents and agent ecosystems
entries.metric: executives agreeing leveraging AI agent ecosystems will be a significant opportunity for their organizations
entries.note: Printed subtitle: 'Ecosystems for AI'. Body: 'Over the next decade, we will see the rise of entire agent ecosystems—large networks of interconnected AI'.

entries.label: The space we need
entries.quote: The spatial computing technology landscape is rapidly growing, but to successfully capitalize on this new medium, enterprises will need to find its killer apps.
entries.subject: Spatial computing
entries.note: Printed subtitle: 'Creating value in new realities'. Survey: 92% of executives agree their organization plans to create a competitive advantage leveraging spatial computing (no horizon).

entries.label: Our bodies electronic
entries.quote: A suite of technologies – from eye-tracking to machine learning to BCI – are starting to understand people more deeply, and in more human-centric ways.
entries.subject: Human interfaces (eye tracking, BCI, neurotech)
entries.note: Printed subtitle: 'A new human interface'. Present-tense consumer survey: 31% of consumers are often frustrated that technology fails to understand them.
